title: Ordinary henselization under a quasi-finite local map
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map of finite type, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be primes with $\mathfrak q$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, and assume $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Write $A_{\mathfrak p}^h$ and $B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ for ordinary henselizations [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then the canonical map $A_{\mathfrak p}^h\to B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ is finite and local, and $B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ is canonically the localization of $A_{\mathfrak p}^h\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\mathfrak q}$ at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}^h$ and $H=B_{\mathfrak q}^h$. The local map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ and the henselian-local structure on $H$ give, by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], the canonical local map $h:R\to H$ over $A\to B$; its residue-field map is the canonical map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Set $C=R\otimes_A B$ and let $\epsilon:C\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ be induced by the residue map of $R$ and $B\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; write $\mathfrak n=\ker\epsilon$ and $D=C_{\mathfrak n}$. The contraction of $\mathfrak n$ to $B$ is $\mathfrak q$, and its contraction to $R$ is the maximal ideal of $R$.

source.place: Tag 05WP, proof setup; Tag 04GN/04GQ, henselization universal property and functorial map

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-four-rings] to the square with original map $A\to B$, base change $A\to R$, and $C=R\otimes_A B$. The tensor map $B\otimes_A R\to C$ is the symmetry isomorphism, so the surjectivity hypothesis holds; the contraction of $\mathfrak n$ to $B$ is $\mathfrak q$. Since $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ (hence of finite type by [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]), the conclusion is that $R\to C$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tag 05WP proof, first paragraph, using Tag 00PN (four-rings lemma)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-type-product-decomposition] to the finite-type map $R\to C$. It decomposes $C\cong A_1\times\cdots\times A_s\times C_0$, with each $A_i$ local and finite over $R$, while $C_0$ is not quasi-finite over $R$ at primes over the maximal ideal. The prime $\mathfrak n$ cannot lie on $C_0$ by Step 2, so it lies on some $A_i$. The corresponding prime of $A_i$ is maximal: its quotient is a finite-dimensional domain over the residue field of $R$, hence a field. Therefore $D=C_{\mathfrak n}\cong A_i$ is finite and local over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-henselian], $D$ is henselian.

source.place: Tag 05WP proof, second paragraph, using Tags 04GJ and 04GH

proof.text: Both $D$ and $H$ are ind-etale over $B$. For $H$ this is [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale] applied to $(B,\mathfrak q)$. For $D$, [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale] gives $A\to R$ ind-etale; [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] gives ind-etaleness after base change to $C$ and after composition with the localization $C\to D$. Explicitly, $C_{\mathfrak n}=\varinjlim_{f\notin\mathfrak n}C_f$; the principal-localization clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] makes each $C\to C_f$ etale of finite presentation, so this is an ind-etale presentation as in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

source.place: Tag 05WP proof, third paragraph; Tag 04GN property (2); Tag 00U2 localization and Tag 097K ind-etale composition

proof.text: The map $C\to H$ given by $r\otimes b\mapsto h(r) b$ sends $\mathfrak n$ into the maximal ideal of $H$, hence factors uniquely through a local $B$-algebra map $D\to H$. Conversely, since $H$ is ind-etale over $B$, the henselian-local target $D$ and the identity residue map $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ give by [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] a unique local $B$-algebra map $H\to D$. The same lemma applied in the other direction gives uniqueness of $D\to H$; both composites induce the identity on the common residue field and are therefore identities by uniqueness. Thus $D\cong H$ compatibly with $R\to H$.

source.place: Tag 05WP proof, final uniqueness paragraph; Tags 08HQ and 08HR

proof.text: Finally, every element of $B\setminus\mathfrak q$ maps outside $\mathfrak n$, so the localization $C_{\mathfrak n}$ already inverts the denominators used to form $B_{\mathfrak q}$. Since $R=A_{\mathfrak p}^h$ is an $A_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra, $C$ identifies with $R\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B$, and the universal properties of localization give a canonical isomorphism $D\cong (R\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\mathfrak q})_{\mathfrak q}$, where the displayed prime is the one induced by $\mathfrak q$. Transporting the finite local map $R\to D$ across $D\cong H$ proves both assertions of the item.
